verdict.rationale: Restate ships its own testing companion library for the TypeScript SDK. It uses Testcontainers to spin up a throwaway Restate Server in Docker for exercising handlers, and the docs also cover a local development setup on the single binary, giving an isolated server instance separate from production. However, the docs only frame this as handler testing. Nothing says production data or the side effects of handlers (such as real HTTP or database calls inside ctx.run) are isolated, and it is only documented for TypeScript. Missing for 10: an explicit sandbox or production-isolation guarantee, isolation of external side effects, documented testing support for other SDKs, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data

citations.quote: This uses [Testcontainers](https://testcontainers.com/) to run a Restate Server in a Docker container and let you test your Restate handlers.
The Typescript SDK has a companion library which makes it easy to test against a Restate container
Learn how to set up your local Restate development environment.
